approach.method_basis: The Parent searches a persistent forest of molecular edit paths rooted in the supplied initial molecules. It purchases the first eligible frontier directly, with no extra rollout edits, and backs each accepted score up only along its actual path. Completed returns, remembered branch peaks and pending evaluations are kept separately. Similarity-weighted peak returns select both initial roots and deeper branches; pending-aware exploration and progressive widening allocate further graph edits.
approach.novelty: Integrate the previously measured root-mean selector into this direct-frontier Parent: choose an initial root by its similarity-weighted mean return while keeping peak selection deeper in the tree. The earlier root-mean sibling retained two rollout edits, while the direct-frontier sibling retained peak selection everywhere; their combination has not been measured. The hypothesis is that broader root allocation can expose useful frontier feedback without losing sustained refinement. The root-mean source lost late conversion and increased receipt and cell concentration, so those competing observations remain part of the test.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-85acb9fe7124 exposes genuine frontier scores but still concentrates root allocation and leaves most scored frontiers without later use. Complete Search evidence gives mean 0.34810111812588734 (SD 0.044753851725843695), 2,822 singleton nonroot occurrences out of 4,488, and 1,359 of 4,350 scored frontiers with actual later-announcement decision/descendant use. The present read-only receipt audit finds 141/150 initial roots followed, only 112/150 followed late, mean root-purchase HHI 0.33054934601664687, and 3,833/4,514 root choices that differ from the passive same-state S/D winner. This is exposure to a concrete selector change, not evidence of unpurchased outcomes. Full/late incumbent-increment masses are 2.094135106253672/1.0992744001720967. The separate root-mean source n-7532fea6b682, on common ancestor n-5cc901d1a9e3 with two suffix transitions, changes 3,207/4,358 root choices, follows all 150 roots and gains +0.030771963496780314 in mean; nevertheless its late mass falls from 1.073893493946193 to 0.5476200808776995 and maximum receipt/cell shares rise from 0.23560362766312273/0.2591713252072214 to 0.2550747583038979/0.38331661551286095. These source findings motivate only the frozen conditional combination; they do not establish additivity or inherited root-mean execution. Evidence: policy/nodes/n-85acb9fe7124.json, policy/nodes/n-7532fea6b682.json, policy/nodes/n-5cc901d1a9e3.json, and policy/scratch/r0054-00-improve-L01-plan/audit-evidence-manifest.json, whose fifteen task/seed audits cite and hash every underlying Search log, trajectory, summary and run.log.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse r54-observed-frontier-reuse-and-feedback-access-review and its recorded queries; no new search is claimed. The retained Single-Player Monte-Carlo Tree Search source is contextual evidence about promising-line concentration and loss of breadth, as recorded in that review, not the origin of this combination. B1 is the actual zero-rollout Parent root concentration and incomplete later frontier use. B3 is the source root-mean panel: broader roots and favorable full endpoints coexist with worse late conversion and receipt/cell concentration. Implement only the frozen root-mean/direct-frontier integration, retain these competing observations, and measure the conditional joint outcome without importing the review's restart or regional-allocation methods.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The frozen review is reused for context and contrary conditions only. The concrete intervention comes from the independently measured direct-frontier source n-85acb9fe7124 and root-mean source n-7532fea6b682 on their common ancestor n-5cc901d1a9e3. Their code and complete Search receipts support a mechanically compatible but scientifically untested combination. No paper element, source performance, restart, width schedule, game heuristic or new asset is adopted.

hypothesis: Conditional integration of the measured shared-mean virtual-root consumer with the Parent direct-frontier controller. For parent_id == 0 only, use S/D (or the inherited neutral 0.5 when D=0) in exploitation; for every parent_id != 0 retain B/D. D=sum_j K_ij*N_j, S=sum_j K_ij*W_j, B=sum_j K_ij*N_j*M_j over N_j>0 and P=sum_j K_ij*O_j remain exactly inherited. Retain the 0.5*sqrt(2*log(max(2,N_parent+O_parent))/(D+P)) bonus, D+P==0 priority and earliest occurrence tie rule. Root mean can reduce domination by isolated remembered peaks, spreading real direct-frontier purchases across initial roots and enabling more useful later refinement without altering deeper peak selection. Zero successful suffix transitions, path-local accepted-only credit and all generation/admission laws remain capabilities of the actual Parent. This one code-Parent experiment measures the combination conditional on zero rollout, not independent effects or a numerical sum of source effects.

finding_summary.headline: Root spreading worked, but useful refinement weakened and mean score fell by 0.06587
finding_summary.insights:
This experiment separates successful redistribution from useful search. The root selector clearly changes allocation, and more distinct frontiers receive later paid follow-up, yet the total amount and value of descendant refinement decline. That refutes the registered integration benefit and its sustained-conversion explanation on this panel. It does not refute the selector’s ability to broaden coverage, the Parent’s direct-frontier mechanism, or every possible tree-search intervention. The earlier root-mean source already showed a late-gain loss under a different rollout condition; its favorable whole-run score cannot be added to the direct-frontier result. This conditional combination supplies contrary measured evidence, without rewriting either source verdict or establishing causal mediation by a particular route.

The method’s limitation is not a lack of graph variety alone. Deeper decisions fell from 6,986 to 5,702, and 2,757 of 4,525 nonroot occurrences still received only one completed return. Molecular assessment finds hundreds of scaffolds per objective but repeated high-scoring use of inherited aromatic scaffold families, with useful coordinated aromatic and nitrogen-containing arrangements reached by the Parent sometimes absent from the Child’s upper tail. Tiny fragments and oversized joins persist: 468 proposals have fewer than six heavy atoms and 177 exceed fifty, versus 432 and 165 for the Parent. These observations support a limitation in converting broad graph edits into useful connected molecular arrangements; they do not establish global scaffold collapse, an absent atom type, or chemical stability from a score. A proposal scheme that preserves and recombines useful connected groups, or an allocation scheme that learns which branches support repeatable descendant gain, could address that kind of limitation. Neither alternative was tested here, and broader coverage or a numerical retune alone is not evidence that it would work. No literature component was newly adopted: this was an internal-evidence combination, with the recorded source paper serving only as context.
finding_summary.results:
The selector ran correctly in all fifteen sessions. It changed 3,439 of 4,565 root decisions while preserving deeper peak selection, zero rollout and exact accepted/pending credit. Root follow-up broadened from 141 to 149 of 150 supplied roots, and late follow-up from 112 to 149. Purchase concentration fell in every session, with mean root HHI dropping from 0.33055 to 0.18002. More paid frontiers were later selected on a route that produced an accepted descendant: 1,550 versus 1,359. But those routes yielded fewer descendant purchases, 3,070 versus 3,191, and less associated gain, 0.67517 versus 1.18928. Full-budget gain per purchase fell from 0.00048141 to 0.00025426; late-budget gain fell from 0.00050541 to 0.00020497. Thus wider access did not produce the predicted sustained useful conversion.

Mean endpoint score fell from 0.34810 to 0.28223, a paired loss of 0.06587 against the registered minimum gain of 0.002. All three seed means fell, by 0.06635, 0.12582 and 0.00546. Seven task/seed endpoints improved and eight worsened; the largest loss was 0.60485 on docking seed 1, and all three sitagliptin endpoints declined. Concentration remains mixed: paired root gain HHI and the largest cell share fell, while the largest single-receipt share rose slightly from 16.60% to 16.82%. The formal Anchor mean remains 0.60703. All sessions completed; no technical failure explains the loss.

molecular.headline: Aromatic, multiring scaffold derivatives coexist with tiny fragments, oversized joins and chemically fragile heteroatom linkages.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-ae947f0cf21c emits phenyl-substituted pyrazolines and thiourea-like groups, methoxyindole carboxamides, fused nitrogenous diones, aryl chromenones, sulfonamides and saturated oxygen-rich protected-sugar-like rings. These are recognizable chemical frameworks, with broad graph diversity, but the higher-scoring subsets repeatedly return to a few supplied scaffold families. The digest ring-closure rates are 0.7552 to 0.8759 and aromatic-token rates are 0.5701 to 0.7874; these are molecule-level SMILES-text indicators, not fractions of aromatic atoms. RDKit readings of accepted optimizer trajectories give task medians of 23 to 29 heavy atoms, with observed extremes of 1 and 94. Of 4350 accepted optimizer molecules, 468 have fewer than 6 heavy atoms and 177 exceed 50, compared with 432 and 165 in published Parent n-85acb9fe7124. Late optimizer ordinals 146 through 290 retain 224 small and 119 large cases, versus Parent 240 and 108, so neither tail disappears. There are 121 molecules with an O-O bond and 155 with a directly bonded N/O/S-halogen pair; these counts may overlap and are structural flags, not measured instability. Ordinary indole amides and aryl heterocycles look synthetically more credible than the peroxides, heteroatom-halogen species, extended nitrogen chains and elaborate joined scaffolds, but no synthesis, stability, exposure or binding experiment is available. Explicit charge and stereocentre token rates are zero in every digest task; this does not imply absence of ionizable atoms or stereogenic centres. RDKit flags unspecified tetrahedral centres in 2337 optimizer molecules. Scope: both Child evaluation and Parent pairing are complete in context.comparison, with Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 and all five tasks. All 30 listed Child/Parent trajectory files were read and contain 300 accepted records each, including 10 initial observations; no trajectory or paired task comparison is missing. These trajectories describe accepted molecules, not rejected attempts. Final digest entries are the last proposals, not necessarily the final incumbents. Evidence and reproducible descriptors are in policy/scratch/r0054-00-improve-L01-molecular/evidence-manifest.json and policy/scratch/r0054-00-improve-L01-molecular/chemistry-summary.json. The manifest lists each audit-seed-N-task.json and its hash alongside the exact underlying trajectory file and SHA256. Published Parent paths are authoritative. Child paths are the frozen request's trusted staging files; their prospective run-relative archive paths are explicitly marked unpublished rather than treated as existing evidence. All comparisons below are descriptive chemistry associations in this Search panel, without mechanism activation or component attribution.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring molecules are compact phenolic diaryl pyrazolines bearing acylated thiourea-like groups, and methoxy/methyl indole carboxanilides. The three seed incumbents have 24, 24 and 25 heavy atoms and three rings, contrasting with the full optimizer range of 1 to 78 heavy atoms. Aromatic and ring-closure token rates are 0.7828 and 0.8759. The ordinary amide and pyrazoline frameworks are plausible synthetic targets; the brominated hydroxy-aminal analogue and complex late joins are less convincing as stable end products. Parent also reached indole/thioamide and aryl nitrogen-rich families, so the Child does not demonstrate a new broad chemical class.
liabilities: The high-scoring CC(O)(Br)N-bearing analogue has an unusual brominated hydroxy-aminal centre; the phenoxyamine analogue adds an O-N linkage. Neither score establishes stability or a practical synthesis.
There are 59 accepted optimizer molecules below 6 heavy atoms and 21 above 50; fragmentation and large polyacetal joins coexist with the compact higher-scoring series.
missing_features: Consistent access to compact, chemically conservative variants preserving the observed aryl/phenol and amide or thiourea geometry is incomplete; late trajectories still leave this useful size and topology region.

The substituted saturated pyrazoline centres remain stereochemically unspecified. Their score benefit from resolving stereochemistry is unmeasured, so this is a representation gap rather than a demonstrated objective requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; replacing one methoxy with methyl gives 0.36371550417720466. The compact N-acetyl thiourea-like diaryl pyrazoline reaches 0.4463521672202675, whereas the initial N-phenyl analogue scores 0.1501184006136499. A fluorinated aryl congener scores 0.41003927643747895, so more halogenation is not a monotone advantage. Both the tiny FF proposal and an enormous joined indole/thiocarbonyl/polyacetal proposal score 0.0. This finite set favors retaining a compact aromatic/polar arrangement while adjusting terminal groups; it does not identify the hidden objective's required pharmacophore. Seed incumbent Child/Parent pairs are 0.36371550417720466/0.3957609793331631, 0.4463521672202675/0.4238198477630873 and 0.36941374410829103/0.37487325032997193: the chemistry comparison is mixed.

per_task.generated_character: The upper score range contains fused N-heterocyclic diones with ester, phenol and aniline substituents; decorated indole carboxamides; and aryl chromenone/nitrile/sulfonamide assemblies. The seed incumbents span 27, 32 and 50 heavy atoms and two to seven rings. The whole optimizer set has median 26 heavy atoms, 331 distinct nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds and ring/aromatic token rates 0.8253/0.6632. Some ordinary aryl amide and heterocycle examples are plausible; the near-top acyl O-F species and densely joined polycycles make overall synthetic plausibility questionable. Parent upper-scoring output used similar indole, thioamide and chromenone neighbourhoods.
liabilities: The acyl O-F molecule is an unusual reactive-bond candidate, and peroxide or hypohalite-like small molecules are admitted at the floor score.

The optimizer includes 92 molecules below 6 heavy atoms and 43 above 50, including 36 of the latter in the late half; a relatively favorable score can accompany considerable aromatic bulk and synthetic complexity.
missing_features: Chemically conservative alternatives that retain the favorable polar/heteroaromatic arrangement while replacing fragile terminal bonds are not established by the high-score sample.

The high-score structures show mainly decoration and joining of familiar starting families; broad graph diversity does not establish equally broad coverage of distinct, stable scaffold arrangements with the same useful functional-group geometry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Adding an aniline amino group to the initial ester/phenol/fused-dione framework changes the observed score from 0.548381482770623 to 0.572328931572629. An aryl-to-aza-aryl substitution on the initial chromenone series is associated with 0.5418375031378128 versus 0.5637456628742032. A much larger seven-ring sulfonamide/chromenone assembly scores 0.5715723551778126, and an acyl O-F-bearing indole assembly scores 0.5712842388863942. These observations support useful polar/heteroaromatic decoration, not a universal smaller-is-better rule. COOC and OOCl both sit at 0.5, the observed score floor, while the task median is 0.515594; the floor cannot distinguish medicinal plausibility. Child/Parent incumbent pairs are 0.572328931572629/0.5619968267027091, 0.5567351200835364/0.5560224089635855 and 0.5715723551778126/0.5615419466888167.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring Child series is dominated by chlorinated, methoxylated diaryl alkenes carrying amides, sometimes with a third aromatic ring or an N-methylpiperidine/hydroxamate appendage. This is accompanied by small phenols, substituted protected oxygen heterocycles and pyrazoline/thioamide derivatives. The seed incumbents are a 37-heavy-atom aryl alkene containing an acyl chloride and tertiary alkyl bromide, an 8-heavy-atom dihydroxybenzene, and a 28-heavy-atom diaryl alkene bearing an N-bromomethyl amide. Ring/aromatic token rates are 0.7552/0.5954. The overall range is 1 to 94 heavy atoms. Ordinary phenols and aryl amides are recognizable chemistry; several lead structures carry reactive handles or unresolved alkene geometry.
liabilities: Acyl chloride, N-bromomethyl, alkyl bromide, hydroperoxide and O-Br examples raise chemical stability and synthetic-handling concerns; the upper score range does not certify them.
The 123 sub-6-heavy-atom and 45 above-50-heavy-atom molecules exceed Parent counts of 83 and 23 in this task. Tiny fragments and highly elaborated joins coexist without a consistent size advantage.
missing_features: Repeated coverage of spatially organized aryl/polar/basic-nitrogen combinations comparable to the strong Parent example is missing from the Child upper tail. A Child piperidine-containing example exists, so adding a basic nitrogen alone is not a supported prescription.

Stable, less halogen-reactive analogues with preserved aryl and amide geometry are not shown to reproduce the strongest Child scores; the current molecules do not identify a unique required receptor pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The diaryl alkene with N-bromomethyl amide scores 0.16834103901310998. A related aryl alkene joined to an N-methylpiperidine amide/hydroxamate scores 0.15812929556456484, while the small dihydroxybenzene reaches 0.07814799147691331. At the lower end, a brominated hydroxyalkyl acyl-thiourea pyrazoline scores 0.00005450172308483119 and a chlorophenyl methyl sulfone scores 0.00011055855856928595. Thus size, sulfur groups, halogen content and ring count alone do not explain the gradient. Published Parent seed 1 instead reached a polyaryl, multiply aminated molecule with an N-substituted pyrrolidine and score 0.6829939673069022, though it also contains an alkyl bromide and aminal-like centres. Child/Parent incumbent pairs are 0.045916010786873955/0.09970328429029204, 0.07814799147691331/0.6829939673069022 and 0.16834103901310998/0.16662005665018462. This suggests incomplete access to useful combinations of aromatic groups and potentially basic nitrogen, not absence of amines or proof of a particular binding interaction.

per_task.generated_character: The upper score range largely retains the initial aryl ester/fused N-heterocyclic dione family, with extra ring closure, ring-nitrogen replacement, ester changes or phenoxyamine substitution. Other high examples couple methoxyindole/phenyl units to cyclic dicarbonyl nitrogen heterocycles. The seed incumbents have 31 heavy atoms and four or five rings. The full optimizer median is 29 heavy atoms, and ring/aromatic token rates are 0.8759/0.7874. There are 390 nonempty typed scaffolds, compared with Parent 359, so useful-family concentration must not be mistaken for global structural collapse. The ordinary heterocyclic dione and ester cores look credible; additional bridged closures and N-O derivatives need route and stability assessment.
liabilities: The additional ring closures increase geometric and synthetic complexity; SMILES validity alone does not establish that the bridged products are accessible.
Phenoxyamine/N-hydroxy motifs and unspecified stereochemistry persist, together with 71 molecules below 6 heavy atoms and 46 above 50.
missing_features: Repeated high-scoring alternatives that preserve the observed aromatic and dicarbonyl relationships while substantially changing the inherited scaffold are limited, despite broad whole-trajectory scaffold diversity.

The sampled gradient does not establish an unobserved target motif. Controlled rearrangement of ring connections and donor/acceptor spacing is an evidence-supported coverage gap, not proof that more rings or a specific new heterocycle is required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial dione/phenol/ester scores 0.1678386594791329. Closing an additional aryl ether ring gives 0.17925526997923785; an added heteroaromatic nitrogen gives 0.17425776739131107, and a phenoxyamine congener gives 0.17149858514250882. These are modest variations on an already useful framework rather than a broad monotone reward for molecular enlargement. C=N, C#C and NCl score 0.0, and the final small piperidine hydroxamate proposals score 0.0690980159557318 and 0.06359922316914202. Within these observations, retaining the aromatic/dicarbonyl framework is more favorable than fragmenting it to small polar pieces. Child/Parent incumbent pairs are 0.17425776739131107/0.1678386594791329, 0.17925526997923785/0.17149858514250882 and 0.1678386594791329/0.17425776739131107; Child seed 2 never exceeds its initial molecule.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring molecules are compact nitrogen-rich diaryl pyrazolines, a pyridyl pyrazoline bearing lactate ester and thiourea-like substitution, and methoxyindole carboxamides with contracted or reduced terminal aryl groups. The leading molecule has 20 heavy atoms, three rings, a phenol and an extended consecutive N-N chain. Other upper-tail examples include an amino-trimethoxyphenyl enone and an N-fluoro-N-methyl indole carboxamide. The full optimizer median is 23 heavy atoms, with ring/aromatic token rates 0.7609/0.5701. Ordinary indole amides and lactate esters are recognizable targets, but the extended nitrogen chains, N-F bond and strained fluorocyclobutenyl substituent make the sampled high-score chemistry uneven.
liabilities: Extended N-N sequences, the N-fluoroamide, an enone and a strained fluorocyclobutenyl substituent are distinct chemical liabilities or questions; scores do not measure their reactivity, stability or biological selectivity.
There are 123 accepted molecules below 6 heavy atoms and 22 above 50, versus Parent 88 and 16. The late half still has 59 small and 13 large examples, and stereogenic centres are left unspecified.
missing_features: Stable compact nitrogen-rich alternatives that retain the observed polar and aromatic relationships without consecutive nitrogen chains or N-halogen bonds are not established across the upper-scoring series.

The output has not demonstrated reliable joint control of size, heteroatom placement and saturated-ring geometry. Both small weakly scoring pyrazolines and oversized near-zero joins remain, so neither contraction alone nor heteroatom addition alone fills the gap.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The NNN-substituted diaryl pyrazoline scores 0.2931485974255099, versus 0.04897968641247111 for the shorter NN-substituted congener observed in another seed and 0.000000000000004620656635650526 for the initial bulky phenyl-thiourea derivative. The pyridyl pyrazoline/lactate ester reaches 0.16691443774635106, while a compact methyl indole carboxamide scores 0.07454576727466115 and its N-fluoro-N-methyl analogue 0.07946682748526555. These observations associate trimming bulky appendages and changing nitrogen/polar-group arrangements with higher scores, but do not establish that reactive N-N or N-F bonds are necessary. Large polyacetal/aryl joined structures score 0.0, and the last simple N-methyl phenylpyrazoline scores only 0.00000000034332323367569257, so compactness without the useful polar arrangement is insufficient. Child/Parent incumbent pairs are 0.07946682748526555/0.3421178198486577, 0.16691443774635106/0.22214762395800358 and 0.2931485974255099/0.3203237480399838. Parent upper molecules also contain unusual thiocarbonyl or nitrogen-rich functionality; the comparison does not establish superior Parent synthesis feasibility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ae947f0cf21c versus published code Parent n-85acb9fe7124, complete frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 in the same profile epoch, 300 accepted records per session with 290 optimizer proposals. Across the accepted optimizer panel, 468 molecules have fewer than 6 heavy atoms and 177 exceed 50, versus Parent 432 and 165. The late half still contains 224 small and 119 large molecules. Observed higher-scoring molecules include compact aryl/amide and pyrazoline arrangements, but also a larger functionalized aryl heterocycle; size alone has no universal direction. See policy/scratch/r0054-00-improve-L01-molecular/evidence-manifest.json and chemistry-summary.json in that same scratch directory.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful connected ring and polar-group arrangements while changing molecular size.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide de novo size-changing transformations that retain informative connected frameworks and donor/acceptor relationships, and let accepted current-session feedback determine useful elaboration. This chemistry association does not justify fixed target sizes, an added reward, a library of benchmark answers or attribution to one controller component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ae947f0cf21c on the complete frozen Search panel, compared descriptively with n-85acb9fe7124 under the same profile. The Child contains 121 O-O-bearing molecules and 155 molecules with direct N/O/S-halogen bonds; these are overlapping structural flags, not measured instability rates. Upper-scoring examples include an acyl O-F group, N-fluoroamide, brominated aminal-like centre and consecutive nitrogen chain, while ordinary amides, phenols and heteroaromatic alternatives also occur. The Parent likewise contains unusual reactive functionality, so this is a persistent output limitation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks reliable access to chemically conservative alternatives around structures whose favorable scores accompany fragile bonds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stable linker, terminal-group and heteroatom substitutions accessible while preserving a promising molecule's geometry and functional-group relationships. Evaluate such alternatives only through the current session's accepted labels. Do not infer that a fragile bond causes the score, or replace oracle feedback with unvalidated chemical-quality penalties.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ae947f0cf21c, complete matched Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 versus n-85acb9fe7124, under the frozen batch and budget. Each Child task contains hundreds of nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds, but the upper-scoring samples repeatedly use inherited indole amides, pyrazolines, fused nitrogenous diones and aryl alkene families. Parent chemistry includes a strong polyaryl/saturated-amine arrangement not reproduced in the corresponding Child upper tail. A Child N-methylpiperidine example is present, so lack of basic nitrogen is not a categorical explanation. Scaffold coverage increases in one comparison and decreases in others; the observations do not support a global diversity-collapse claim.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad graph diversity does not consistently translate into useful alternative scaffold arrangements or coordinated aromatic, polar and ionizable groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable controlled changes to ring connections, linker lengths, saturation and heteroatom placement that preserve useful group relationships, rather than relying on extra atom types or bulk alone. This is a generator coverage hypothesis for de novo, task-agnostic search; the appropriate arrangement must emerge from session feedback, and no target-specific pharmacophore or component benefit is established.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ae947f0cf21c frozen digest and full Search trajectories, all three frozen seeds and all supplied sessions; published Parent n-85acb9fe7124 is the comparison baseline. Explicit stereocentre-token rates are zero throughout the Child digest, while RDKit identifies unspecified tetrahedral stereocentres in 2337 accepted optimizer molecules. The structures include substituted pyrazolines, protected oxygen-rich rings and branched aminal-like centres. Formal charge tokens are also absent, but potentially ionizable nitrogen is present; token absence does not establish a protonation or charge requirement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted structures do not resolve stereochemical alternatives introduced by saturated, fused and branched molecular edits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where compatible with the existing evaluator identity contract, preserve and distinguish meaningful stereochemical states introduced by graph edits. Any performance benefit requires new measured evidence; the absence of stereo tokens does not authorize a target-specific stereoisomer, charge state or extra oracle budget.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
